issues.legal_issue: A counterclaim may be filed after the written statement when its cause of action continued until the time for filing the written statement or its permitted extension.
material_facts: A defendant applied to file a counterclaim after filing a written statement in a pending civil suit.
The application was made on a cause of action alleged to have arisen before or after the suit was instituted and to have continued until the written statement or the extended time for filing it.
The lower court held that the application was not barred merely because it was filed after the written statement.
issues.conclusion: The application was not ex facie barred by Order VIII Rule 6A of the Code of Civil Procedure, and the order allowing it to proceed was not interfered with.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order VIII Rule 6A of the Code of Civil Procedure, the right to file a counterclaim is referable to the accrual of its cause of action. Following Mahendra Kumar v. State of Madhya Pradesh, a counterclaim may be filed after the written statement if its cause of action arose before or after institution of the suit and continued until the written statement or the extended date for filing it.

predicates.defendant_counterclaim_in_pending_civil_: A defendant in a pending civil suit seeks to bring a counterclaim in that proceeding.
predicates.counterclaim_filed_after_written_stateme: The defendant files the counterclaim after filing the written statement.
predicates.cause_of_action_continued_until_written_: The cause of action for the counterclaim continued until the written statement was filed or the permitted time for filing it expired.

issues.definition: When a defendant brings a counterclaim in a pending civil suit after the written statement and the counterclaim's cause of action continued through the deadline for filing that statement, the counterclaim may be filed after the written statement.

issues.legal_issue: A limitation objection raised for the first time on appeal cannot be determined without the relevant factual materials and where the lower court has not considered it.
material_facts: The appellant argued for the first time before the Supreme Court that the cause of action had arisen long before the suit and that the suit and counterclaim were time-barred.
The limitation issue had not been raised before the lower court and had not been examined there.
The Court stated that limitation, if raised, should be decided after the date of accrual of the cause of action is determined from relevant materials.
issues.conclusion: The Court expressed no opinion on the limitation contention and left it to be decided on relevant materials.
issues.legal_principle: Whether a claim is barred by limitation depends on determining the accrual date of the cause of action from relevant materials; the Court did not decide the limitation contention raised for the first time on appeal.

predicates.limitation_objection_first_raised_on_app: A party raises a limitation objection for the first time before the appellate court.
predicates.lower_court_did_not_consider_limitation: The lower court did not examine the limitation objection.
predicates.accrual_date_requires_relevant_materials: Determining when the cause of action accrued requires consideration of relevant factual materials.

issues.definition: When a limitation objection is first raised on appeal, was not considered below, and depends on relevant materials to establish accrual, the limitation issue is left for determination on those materials.
